stories.headline: ‘Who approved it?’: HI president Dilip Tirkey seeks answers on jersey switch
stories.deck: Hockey India president Dilip Tirkey questions the director general's authority. He seeks accountability and transparency in the recent jersey colour change. Tirkey expressed surprise at learning about the redesign through social media. He emphasised the need for governance and consultation for symbolic decisions. The president requested a comprehensive reply with documentary evidence by Tuesday.
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU: What began as a controversy over the Indian hockey team’s switch from its traditional blue jersey to saffron has now snowballed into a governance battle within Hockey India (HI).
In a strongly worded letter to the federation’s director general (DG), Cdr RK Srivastava, HI president Dilip Tirkey has raised serious questions over authority, accountability and transparency in the decision-making process behind the jersey change.
The letter, accessed by TOI, is Tirkey’s response to Srivastava’s July 31 explanation on the approval process. Questioning who authorised the redesign and whether due process was followed, Tirkey has sought answers from the federation’s administrative leadership, deepening the controversy.
Describing the DG’s four-page reply as largely off the point, Tirkey wrote: “...the issue under consideration is not merely the colour or design of a playing jersey. The matter concerns the decision-making process adopted for a change involving one of the most recognisable symbols of Indian hockey, the authority under which such a decision was taken, the consultations undertaken, compliance with Hockey India’s governance framework, and whether appropriate institutional processes were followed.
”
The former India captain added: “Hockey India is a custodian of a legacy. Decisions affecting such symbols must therefore be approached with the highest standards of governance, transparency and accountability.”
Tirkey also questioned why the elected Executive Board was bypassed. Revealing that he learnt about the redesigned jersey only through a WhatsApp group message a few hours before its social media launch on July 27, Tirkey wrote: “The Director General has an important executive and administrative role in managing the affairs of Hockey India and implementing approved decisions. However, administrative responsibility cannot be interpreted as replacing or overriding the authority of the elected governance bodies. Given the importance and national significance of the decision, the Executive Board requires clarification as to why the President and the Executive Board were not consulted before the public announcement.”
The 412-cap India veteran also took exception to a section of the DG’s reply that detailed HI’s high-performance initiatives.
“The Executive Board is fully familiar with the demands of elite sport and high-performance environments. The EB includes several distinguished former international players and Olympians who have personally experienced the demands of preparing for and performing at the highest levels of hockey... and fully recognises that modern sport requires continuous improvement and that every genuine marginal gain must be pursued,” Tirkey wrote.
With the controversy erupting less than three weeks before the FIH Hockey World Cup begins in the Netherlands and Belgium on Aug 15, Tirkey also questioned the timing of the change.
“A decision intended to improve performance must not inadvertently create uncertainty, distraction or disruption at a critical stage of preparation. It is therefore necessary for the Executive Board to understand how the jersey change was assessed within the overall high-performance plan,” he said.
Tirkey has sought a comprehensive reply from the DG, supported by documentary evidence, by 5 pm on Tuesday.
Signing off, he wrote: “Hockey India does not own Indian hockey. We are trustees and custodians of a national sporting legacy”.
Key clarifications sought:
- Whether the potential impact of the jersey change on athlete preparation, confidence, comfort, mental focus and competition readiness was assessed
- Whether the coaching staff, sports science team and performance support personnel provided any written assessment regarding the timing of introducing the new kit before the World Cup
- Whether the possible impact of this situation on athlete focus, mental preparation and tournament readiness was assessed before the public announcement.
- Whether sponsors, the Odisha government, were consulted before approval and public unveiling of the new jersey
- Details of any testing or evaluation conducted before the kit was introduced in international competition
- If any player experiences difficulty with the new kit during competition, please provide details of the alternative arrangements or corrective measures available

stories.headline: Shoulder surgery, 7 months out, one throw: How Yash Vir Singh won CWG bronze
stories.deck: Yash Vir Singh arrived in Glasgow with little attention but left with a Commonwealth Games bronze after a personal-best final throw. In this interview with TimesofIndia.com, he opens up about the injury that nearly derailed his career, the months spent in rehabilitation, Neeraj Chopra's words before his medal-winning attempt and the father who has guided him since his first throws with a bamboo…
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Before Yash Vir Singh walked up for his sixth and final throw in the men's javelin final at Scotstoun Stadium, two voices stayed with him.
One came from Olympic champion Neeraj Chopra.
"You're throwing well. Just keep it straight and believe in yourself. It's your last throw, just make sure you don't foul. You can do it."
The other came from his father and coach, Rai Singh.
"It's the last throw. Put everything into it."
Seconds later, the javelin landed at 85.41 metres.
Yash Vir leapt from seventh place to the bronze medal position, registering a personal best by almost three metres. The effort not only earned him a place on the podium alongside Neeraj Chopra, who took silver behind Sri Lanka's Rumesh Tharanga, but also made him only the third Indian to win a Commonwealth Games medal in men's javelin. For the first time in the history of the event, two Indians shared the Commonwealth Games podium.
The medal came in one of the strongest men's javelin fields assembled at a Commonwealth Games.
The Glasgow final featured one of the strongest javelin fields assembled at a Commonwealth Games. Besides Neeraj and Yash Vir, India also had Rohit Yadav in the final. Reigning Commonwealth Games champion Arshad Nadeem was back to defend his title.
Former world champion Anderson Peters of Grenada, Trinidad and Tobago's Keshorn Walcott and former Commonwealth champion Julius Yego were all in the fray. Rumesh Tharanga, meanwhile, arrived in Glasgow after a series of impressive performances and eventually walked away with gold.
For much of the evening, Yash Vir remained in the background.
Having squeezed into the final in 10th place during qualification, few would have backed the Indian Railways ticket collector to leave Glasgow with a medal. His best throw heading into the final round measured 81.33m, leaving him seventh in the standings with one attempt remaining.
Then came his final attempt.
"I'd made up my mind - today it was do or die. I shouted it out and then went for the throw. It wasn't easy. I'd already committed two fouls and even my fifth throw was only 76.95 metres. My only thought was to produce my personal best. I had nothing to lose. But there was a hunger built up over the last four years. I'll always remember that 85.41m throw. I'm immensely grateful to God," Yash Vir told TimesofIndia.com.
The conditions hardly made life easier. Several leading throwers struggled to find consistency as gusty conditions made it difficult to judge the release. Yash Vir adjusted quickly.
"I quickly calculated the wind conditions. Then I increased my speed a bit and made a slight change to my technique according to the wind pressure. The plan was simple - release the javelin with full power. That's it. The plan worked. I'm happy that I finally crossed the 85-metre mark. My previous best was over 83 metres at the Inter State Championships."
Before Glasgow glory came years of struggle
The bronze medal was the culmination of four years spent fighting through injury, surgery and rehabilitation, all while holding on to a promise he had made to himself.
"Main wapsi karke dikhaunga.[I'll make a comeback]."
The promise was made in 2022.
During a training session, Yash Vir injured his shoulder. The damage was serious. One of the muscles in his rotator cuff - the supraspinatus - had been affected, leaving him in constant pain and eventually requiring surgery at the Abhinav Bindra Targeting Performance (ABTP) Centre in Jaipur.
The operation was successful, but it came with another challenge. Doctors ruled him out of competition for at least seven months. For an athlete whose life revolved around throwing the javelin, the rehabilitation was as much a mental battle as a physical one.
"It was an extremely difficult time. All I wanted was to return to the field," Yash Vir said.
"The surgery went well and my treatment was completed successfully. Dr Harshvardhan Singh and Dr Aditi Thakur are like God to me. They gave me the confidence that I would be able to throw the javelin again the way I always had. Today, I am here because of them. I owe them a lot."
Unable to train, he spent months confined to bed. There was little he could do physically, so he tried to stay connected with the sport in every way possible. He watched videos of his old competitions, relived some of his best throws and immersed himself in motivational books, refusing to let the dream of competing again fade away.
Yash Vir Singh (Special Arrangements)
When he eventually returned in 2023, the signs were encouraging. His comeback competition ended with a silver medal. Strong performances followed over the next two seasons, eventually earning him a place in India's squad for the Commonwealth Games.
Yet, despite steady progress, Yash Vir travelled to Glasgow with little fanfare.
The spotlight naturally remained on Chopra, India's Olympic and world champion, while Rohit Yadav completed the three-member Indian contingent. Yash Vir entered the competition as an outsider, having qualified for the final in 10th place.
The father who never gave up on Yash Vir
Throughout the journey, one person remained at the centre of it all - his father, Rai Singh.
"Now, I don't want to look back. A Commonwealth Games medal means a lot to me. You can say this is just the beginning," he said.
Behind that journey has been one constant figure. His father. Rai Singh is much more than Yash Vir's coach.
A former national-level javelin thrower himself, Rai won multiple national medals and Railway championship titles before becoming an athletics coach with the Indian Railways. An NIS Diploma holder, he has guided his son's career from the very beginning, overseeing not just his technique but every aspect of his routine.
Yash Vir Singh with his father (Special Arrangements)
Long before international medals entered the conversation, father and son spent countless hours training at the Railway Ground near Jaipur railway station.
The first javelin wasn't even made of metal. It was bamboo.
"My father is very strict. He believes in discipline. He takes care of my training, schedule, diet and every single aspect of my life. I may be his son, but he is even stricter with me than anyone else," Yash Vir said.
"Whatever I am today is because of him. Foreign coaches come and go after a while, but it is my father who has taught me everything from the very beginning."
Even now, the technical discussions happen at home.
"I don't know much about biomechanics. My father understands it really well. Whatever plan he gives me, whether it's about intensity, power, run-up or the release angle, everything comes from him."
At Scotstoun Stadium, Rai Singh watched from above the runway, shouting instructions after every attempt. He had never received the opportunity to compete on one of athletics' biggest stages himself.
On Saturday evening in Glasgow, he watched his son stand on the Commonwealth Games podium with a bronze medal around his neck. For Yash Vir, the medal represented a personal best, a national milestone and the fulfilment of a promise he had made to himself four years ago.

stories.headline: Nazara names Raymond Stauffer CEO, rejigs $303 million gaming deal
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Nazara Technologies has appointed Bluetile and BestPlay founder Raymond A Stauffer as its new CEO while revamping its proposed acquisition of the two gaming companies into a $303 million all-cash deal.
Founder Nitish Mittersain will step down as CEO when Stauffer takes charge on Sept 1, subject to regulatory approvals. He will continue as managing director and focus on Nazara’s long-term strategy, portfolio management and key partnerships.
Stauffer will oversee Nazara’s day-to-day operations, including the integration of its portfolio companies and collaboration across product development, artificial intelligence, data, user acquisition and monetisation.
Nazara will acquire 100% of Bluetile and BestPlay at closing for a fixed consideration of $303 million. It will pay $89 million at the first closing, with the remaining $214 million to be paid in agreed instalments by April 1, 2027.
The earlier structure involved acquiring about half the businesses initially for $100.3 million. It also included performance-linked payments of up to $98.2 million and provisions to acquire the remaining stake later. 
The revised deal removes the stock component, future valuation uncertainty and shared ownership.
Bluetile and BestPlay reported revenue of Rs 518 crore and operating profit of Rs 55 crore in the June quarter. Nazara expects to consolidate their financial performance from the Sept quarter, subject to completion of the acquisition.
“Having led the company through two distinct phases of its evolution, I believe this is the right time to strengthen its leadership structure with a dedicated CEO who brings deep international operating experience,” Mittersain said.
Nazara reported a net loss of Rs 82.47 crore for the June quarter, compared with a profit of Rs 51.34 crore a year earlier. Total income declined 24% to Rs 437.55 crore from Rs 575.87 crore. The loss included Rs 62.41 crore as Nazara’s share of losses from associate companies and an impairment charge of Rs 21.81 crore.
Its core gaming revenue, however, rose 14% to Rs 275 crore. The segment posted an operating profit of Rs 54 crore, with a margin of 19.5%. Fusebox, Kiddopia and Animal Jam all reported revenue growth during the quarter.

stories.headline: Row over public urination ends in man’s murder
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 A 29-year-old four-wheeler AC mechanic has been arrested for allegedly killing a 45-year-old cook near Laggere following a trivial argument over public urination.
The accused, Mohammed Yunus, is a resident of Kurubarahalli, while the deceased, Kumar (45), lived in Mahalakshmi Layout.
On the night of July 28, Kumar and his relatives, Nagendra and Narasimhamurthy, had been drinking at a bar. After dropping Nagendra home, Narasimhamurthy returned to pick up Kumar.
While walking through Kempegowda Layout, Kumar stopped to urinate by the roadside. Yunus, who witnessed the act, confronted him, leading to an argument. During the altercation, Yunus allegedly assaulted Kumar.
When Narasimhamurthy arrived, he intervened and asked Kumar to get on the bike. Police said Yunus assaulted Kumar again and pulled him by the shirt collar, causing him to fall onto the road and suffer a fatal head injury.
Kumar was rushed to a nearby private hospital, where he died. Mahalakshmipuram police registered a murder case, examined CCTV footage from the area, and arrested Yunus Sunday.
During interrogation, Yunus allegedly confessed to the assault. He told police he worked as a mechanic at the garage where Kumar had urinated and confronted him because the area often developed a foul smell. He claimed he assaulted Kumar after being abused but had no intention of killing him.

stories.headline: After 2-day hiatus, M’luru-B’luru rail link restored
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 In a major relief for thousands of passengers, rail operations were restored late Monday along the ghat section between Bengaluru and Mangaluru after a two-day standstill.
According to South Western Railway (SWR), the route was cleared for passenger traffic after restoration and safety certification. SWR said a restriction of 10kmph has been placed and loco pilots have been cautioned to dead stop at every station before proceeding ahead.
In its official statement, SWR said: “The track was certified fit 7.25pm. Passengers are advised that minor residual delays may still occur as normal timetables are progressively stabilised.”
Train No. 17378 Mangaluru Central-Vijayapura Express was the first train to cross the section after the landslip. Rail operations between Sakleshpur and Subrahmanya Road were halted Saturday night after mud and debris fell on the track between Yedakumari and Shirivagilu railway stations.
On Monday, SWR’s Mysuru divisional railway manager Mudit Mittal had personally supervised the works at the site, which does not have any approach road to it. 
The 55km-long ghat section is the shortest existing rail link between Mangaluru and the Karnataka capital.
Explaining the challenging conditions, a senior SWR official stated: “There was heavy rain at the location and the forecast was not favourable for the work. Despite that, restoration was happening 24x7 and there was no shortage of labour. Because of rain, mud was sliding down repeatedly, making things a little difficult”, he said.
Significant delays
The landslip along the ghats also led to increased traffic between Bengaluru and Kerala, which forced significant delays for two trains on the route.
Kozhikode-KSR Bengaluru Express, which was supposed to depart Kozhikode at 3.30pm. departed only at 8pm — almost 4.5 hours late. Similarly, Train No. 16511 SMVT Bengaluru-Kozhikode, supposed to depart SMVT at 11.55pm, was shifted to start from Yeshwantpur just hours before its schedule. Officials clarified that both these services had to be replanned because of the pairing train running late.

stories.headline: Delivery exec assaulted, robbed of scooter
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 A 23-year-old food delivery executive was assaulted and robbed of his scooter by three miscreants near Singasandra bus stand on Hosur Main Road last week.
Pavan
, a resident of Garavebhavipalya, told police he was waiting for delivery orders around 11pm on July 30 when the trio approached him from behind and demanded his Honda Dio scooter, registered in his cousin’s name. When Pavan refused, the accused allegedly assaulted him, snatched the scooter keys, a power bank and a charging cable from his pocket, and pushed him to the ground. They then fled with the scooter, which had his food delivery bag attached.
Begur police have registered a case of robbery under BNS Section 309 and launched a search for the accused.

stories.headline: Free is the most expensive word in public policy: Nageswaran
stories.bodyText:
CHENNAI: Flagging that “free is the most expensive word in public policy”, chief economic adviser (CEA) Anantha Nageswaran said infrastructure built on the promise of free or below-cost services cannot attract patient capital. “What makes infrastructure worthy of patient capital? There are three conditions: quality infrastructure, contract certainty, and policy certainty. And the fourth, which we find harder to say aloud: durable returns rest on two things—a price that covers the economic cost of a service, and a public willing to pay a fair charge for it. There is no third way around it,” he said.
Infrastructure built on the promise of free or below-cost service cannot support patient capital. It is a contradiction written into the balance sheet. Someone always ends up paying; either the user pays a fair charge, the taxpayer pays a hidden one, or the asset itself pays through slow decay due to a lack of maintenance. Free is the most expensive word in public policy,” he said at the Tamil Nadu Infrastructure Summit, organised by CII.

stories.headline: Lower min age for MD, directors to 18: Parliamentary panel
stories.deck: A parliamentary panel suggests lowering the minimum director age to eighteen years. The committee also backs raising the maximum director age to seventy-five years. Special NCLT benches for insolvency matters are recommended for efficient asset resolution. The panel proposes retaining the ten crore net profit threshold for CSR applicability. New provisions will enable seamless re-domiciliation of…
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: The joint committee of Parliamentary panel examining the amendments to the Companies Act has recommended reducing the minimum age for appointment as managing director and whole-time director from 21 years to 18, bringing it in line with similar age caps in the US, Singapore, Germany and Australia. It has also backed raising the maximum age from 70 years to 75, without the requirement of a special resolution.
“During the deliberations, a general consensus within the committee arose as to lowering of the minimum age from 21 to 18 years. The ministry (of corporate affairs) has informed that similar suggestions were received from HLC-Niti Aayog in order to encourage and increase the representation of young people on boards...,” the panel chaired by Sudheer Gupta said in the report tabled in Parliament. While supporting further decriminalisation of the law, the committee also recommended dropping some of the proposals that are part of the bill such as doing away with one of the proposals related to NFRA and instead providing a penalty.
The panel backed creating special NCLT benches for specific cases. “Dedicated benches focused solely on insolvency matters would guarantee strict adherence to statutory resolution timelines, which would significantly help to avoid value erosion of distressed assets in IBC cases. 
Simultaneously, this would insulate regular benches from unplanned procedural urgencies, thereby enabling them to devote focused attention to routine corporate reorganisations, mergers, and conversions in a predictable and time-bound manner,” it said.
Besides, the committee has recommended retaining the Rs 10 crore net profit threshold for CSR applicability, while allowing in-kind contributions for small companies, maintaining a negative list of ineligible agencies, and keeping exemption powers strictly with Parliament, instead of delegating it to the executive.
In its over 1,100-page report, the panel proposed insertion of a new chapter to enable “seamless re-domiciliation of foreign companies to IFSC, without requiring winding-up in their home jurisdiction”. It said a significant number of Indian promoters with offshore operations want to return to Indian shores.
“In order to facilitate the reverse-flipping and shifting of foreign subsidiaries of Indian companies back to India, the committee feels that an enabling legal framework including provisions relating to taxation, capital gains, stamp duty, transfer and vesting of assets and liabilities, filing and compliance requirements, continuation of rights and obligations, and other consequential or incidental matters arising from such re-domiciliation, is essential for seamless migration,” the report said.

stories.headline: Changes to boost electronics, investment
stories.deck: New tax law amendments are proposed by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman. These changes aim to offer concessions to overseas investors and boost electronics manufacturing. The government plans to extend tax exemptions for specified electronic goods by ten years. It also introduces new exemptions for storing and selling electronic components. These reforms signal a shift towards long-term…
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman is set to introduce further amendments to tax laws going beyond the Ordinance offering concessions to overseas investors putting money in govt bonds.
According to the bill that has been circulated, it has been proposed to replace the broad reference to “electronic goods” with a defined list of “specified electronic goods” and extend the tax exemption by 10 years—up to tax year 2040-41. 
“This amendment brings greater clarity to the tax exemption available to foreign companies supplying capital goods, equipment or tooling to Indian contract manufacturers engaged in manufacturing specified electronic goods. By expressly defining the eligible product categories, the bill is expected to reduce interpretational disputes, while the extended exemption provides long-term tax certainty for global manufacturers,” said Amit Maheshwari, managing partner at consulting company AKM Global.
There is an expansion and clarification of eligible electronic products covered under the incentive regime, including mobile phones, laptops, tablets, servers, wearables, hearables and other related sub-assemblies.
The bill also proposes to introduce a new tax exemption for foreign companies undertaking the storage and sale of electronic components through customs bonded areas, where such components are supplied to Indian contract manufacturers of specified electronic goods. The exemption, available until 31 March 2041, is subject to prescribed reporting requirements.
Further, conditions for offshore investment funds are proposed to be rationalised by removing several prescriptive eligibility conditions. Further, dividend tax neutrality is proposed to be restored for REIT and InvIT investors.
Govt is proposing tax exemption on income on sale of rough diamonds in the hands of an overseas company, that is engaged in diamond mining or is functioning as a sightholder, broker, aggregator or a tender and auction entity for such business, for 15 years, ending in March, 2041.
“The bill signals a calibrated shift from short-term relief to longer-term competitiveness. While the Ordinance addressed immediate concerns arising from global economic developments, govt has now supplemented those measures with additional reforms following stakeholder consultations… The liberalisation of the fund management regime, incentives for electronics supply chains, facilitation measures for data centres and diamond trading, and tax relief for foreign investors in govt securities collectively point towards a policy objective of attracting global capital and business activity into India. Collectively, the amendments reflect a clear emphasis on investment facilitation, supply-chain resilience and long-term tax certainty,” said Richa Sawhney, tax partner at Grant Thonton Bharat.

stories.headline: AI fraud is hitting India’s new net users hardest: Amazon
stories.deck: Protecting new online shoppers from AI scams is India's next e-commerce challenge. Amazon's trust chief highlights consumer awareness as critical for digital fraud. Generative AI creates sophisticated scams, but also aids detection efforts. Behavioral data helps distinguish genuine sellers from bad actors effectively. Amazon acts against fraud proactively, not waiting for regulatory mandates.
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: India’s next big e-commerce challenge is not artificial intelligence itself but protecting millions of first-time online shoppers from AI-powered scams, according to Amazon’s global trust and safety chief, who said consumer awareness has become as critical as technology in tackling digital fraud.
Rohan Oommen, vice president for customer and partner trust at Amazon, said the rapid influx of new digital commerce users from tier-2 and tier-3 cities has made India distinct from more mature markets, such as the US, where e-commerce adoption has largely plateaued.
“India has a large number of first-time users entering the digital economy. Awareness is much lower, which makes education a significant part of the solution,” Oommen told TOI.
He said generative AI has made fraud more sophisticated by enabling fake identities, forged documents and synthetic reviews, but it has also strengthened Amazon’s ability to detect abuse at scale.
The company is increasingly deploying AI systems, including agentic AI that can carry out continuous audits, while relying on years of behavioural data to distinguish genuine sellers from bad actors. “Behaviour is much harder to fake than documents or images,” Oommen said.
According to Amazon’s latest Trustworthy Shopping Experience Report, the company removed nearly 300 million fake reviews, took down about 70,000 phishing websites, and acted against around 14,000 scam-linked phone numbers globally last year. Oommen said phone-based fraud remains harder to tackle than fake websites because establishing attribution is significantly more difficult.
On platform accountability, he said Amazon does not wait for regulation before acting against fraud.

stories.headline: Consider capping rates on affordable loans: LICHF chief
stories.bodyText:
MUMBAI: The chief of LIC Housing Finance, the largest home loan company in India, has called for capping of interest rates on loans in the affordable housing segment stating that nothing about some of the rates being charged in this segment is affordable. MD and CEO Tribhuwan Adhikari said some housing finance companies are charging interest rates of 15-16% in the affordable housing segment and suggested that the regulator should prescribe a ceiling on spread over funding costs.
“Affordable housing finance is a misnomer because the borrower definitely cannot afford 16%-17%,” he said. He added that Reserve Bank or National Housing Bank could consider capping lending spreads. In the case of banks, RBI links their floating rate to the repo rate. However, Adhikari did not see a case for linking HFC rates to external benchmarks because about half of the sector’s borrowings come from banks. Unless housing finance companies received similar access to low-cost funding, such a move would put them at a disadvantage.
Adhikari said LIC Housing Finance itself is cautiously operating in the affordable housing segment through a “banking surrogate” product that assesses borrowers using bank statements and GST filings instead of income tax returns or salary slips.
On the company’s growth, Adhikari said LIC Housing Finance expects its loan book to stand at around Rs 3.5 lakh crore by the end of FY27. The company’s net profit in Q1FY27 rose 10% to Rs 1,499 crore and loans grew 14% — the strongest in four to five years and the momentum would continue, he said. Its loan book growth has trailed peers because of repayments and prepayments, but LICHF is now focused on accelerating growth while retaining its AUM lead over rivals.

stories.headline: ​FIFA foul: On the shelved FIFA Forward Enterprise
stories.deck: Football’s governing body must embrace fairness, not chase profit
stories.bodyText:
The collapse of FIFA’s controversial plan that would have helped private investors benefit from the World Cup and other flagship competitions represents the latest hit to the global body’s reputation. In the aftermath of the 2026 World Cup, FIFA president Gianni Infantino hurriedly put together strategies to form the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) to consolidate all revenue-generating operations, and invite private bodies to hold non-controlling stakes in the body. But this elicited enormous backlash from a number of FIFA’s 211 member associations, with European governing body UEFA even declaring that its 55 members would boycott the World Cup. Europe is football’s nerve-centre, and with the Asian Football Confederation and players’ union FIFPRO also expressing apprehensions, and one of Mr. Infantino’s senior advisers quitting in protest, the scheme was a non-starter. The episode has also reduced Mr. Infantino’s standing, especially after the controversy-ridden World Cup, where political interference by the U.S. — one of the co-hosts — and rampant commercialisation severely diminished ‘the beautiful game’. The now-shelved FFE was to be backed by a venture capitalist with familial ties to U.S. President Donald Trump, making the whole deal all the more suspect. The 2027 FIFA election, where Mr. Infantino was expected to be re-elected for a third full term, is no longer a cake-walk.
The saga has brought back into focus the conflict at the heart of FIFA’s functioning and the patronage politics it enables. FIFA is the global regulator of the sport, and ideally, its commercial wing should be kept at an arm’s length. However, the organisation’s structure is such that the revenue generated is often used as leverage to extract favour. As a non-profit, FIFA is duty-bound to redistribute income amongst its members, but presidents — past and present — have turned it into a vote-catching tool to hold on to power. To approve the FFE project, FIFA had reportedly offered each of its members $20 million upfront, and a direct beneficiary of this would have been Mr. Infantino at next year’s election, for every association has one vote. However, history shows that moves to use legacy tournaments for self-aggrandisement are bound to fail. In 2018, the International Tennis Federation entered into a 25-year, $3 billion partnership with a private investment firm to re-jig the over-a-century-old Davis Cup, with the promise of extra money for the game’s global development. That agreement lasted just five years, with the shift from the traditional home-and-away format deeply unpopular and considered soul-shattering to the sport. It is time FIFA re-inculcates fairness, embraces consensus and shuns its president’s unilateralism.
Published - August 04, 2026 12:10 am IST

stories.headline: Pochettino to stay as USA coach until 2030 World Cup
stories.deck: The 54-year-old took over in 2024 and led the USA to the last 16 at the recent World Cup, which they co-hosted with Canada and Mexico
stories.bodyText:
Mauricio Pochettino has signed a contract extension to remain the head coach of the United States national team until the 2030 World Cup, U.S. football announced on Monday (August 3, 2026)
The 54-year-old took over in 2024 and led the USA to the last 16 at the recent World Cup, which they co-hosted with Canada and Mexico.
"It has become clear to us that there is tremendous potential to make the men's national team program even stronger," said Argentinian Pochettino, whose coaching staff have also agreed new contracts.
"The passion we experienced from the fans throughout the World Cup only strengthened our belief in what is possible here...”
"We want to try to have a lasting impact on the sport in the country that has welcomed us so warmly and for that impact to extend beyond results on the field."
The Americans won three matches at a World Cup for the first time before being knocked out by Belgium, following a huge controversy over FIFA's decision to suspended striker Folarin Balogun's ban for a red card.
Former Tottenham and Paris Saint-Germain boss Pochettino was named coach two years ago, after previous boss Gregg Berhalter left following a group-stage exit from the 2024 Copa America which the USA hosted.
Pochettino helped turn things around and led the team to the 2025 CONCACAF Gold Cup final, which they lost 2-1 to Mexico.
He had been linked with a return to European club football, but will instead stay with the US until the next World Cup, slated to be largely held in Spain, Portugal, and Morocco.
"Mauricio has built a culture where players trust the group, trust the process and trust each other," said U.S. football president Cindy Parlow Cone.
"We saw the impact of that belief in the way the team grew, competed and performed on the world's biggest stage."
The USA have not reached the quarter-finals of a men's World Cup since 2002, and hopes were high a partisan home crowd could carry them to at least that stage.
But after the Balogun affair, a fired-up Belgium quashed those hopes last month with a crushing 4-1 victory.
Published - August 04, 2026 12:52 am IST

stories.headline: Vozinha arrives in Chile to sign for Colo-Colo
stories.deck: Vozinha, 40, will ‌sign a six-month contract, with the possibility ​of a one-year extension, on Monday (August 3, 2026) after ⁠undergoing a medical and he will start training on Tuesday (August 4)
stories.bodyText:
Cape Verde’s veteran goalkeeper Vozinha, who became a social media sensation at the World Cup, has arrived in Chile to join Colo-Colo.
Vozinha, 40, will sign a six-month contract, with the possibility of a one-year extension, on Monday (August 3, 2026) after undergoing a medical and he will start training on Tuesday (August 4).
Chilean media said he was likely to make his debut on August 16, against O'Higgins as Colo-Colo look to maintain their healthy lead at the head of the Chilean Premier Division.
Vozinha's performances for the small African island nation at the World Cup in North America helped Cape Verde get past the group stage before a narrow loss to Argentina in the last 32. They held eventual winners Spain and twice world champions Uruguay to draws in the group phase and Vozinha played a major role in his country's debut appearance at the global tournament.
His Instagram account went from around 50,000 followers to around 17.4 million after his heroics against Spain in the first week of the tournament in June.
Colo-Colo were on Friday (July 31) granted permission for Vozinha, whose real name is Josimar Jose Evore Dias, to use his footballing nickname on his shirt despite regulations in the South American country prohibiting it.
The possibility he might be banned from using the name he had on his World Cup kit proved less contentious than originally thought, however, with other Chilean clubs agreeing to Colo-Colo's request.
The nickname Vozinha, which means “little grandmother” in Portuguese, was given by the older kids when he was a boy and would cry after losing games of street football and storm home to his grandparents, with whom he lived.
The goalkeeper was last at Portuguese second division side Chaves and has played for clubs in Angola, Cyprus, Moldova and Slovakia.
Published - August 04, 2026 12:42 am IST

stories.headline: UEFA threatens FIFA with legal action over failed plan to sell World Cup stakes
stories.deck: The letter named 18 FIFA executives who it said should retain data, documents and electronic messages as potential evidence. They include Infantino, Zurich-based chief finance officer Thomas Peyer and Arsène Wenger, the coaching great who is FIFA's head of global soccer development
stories.bodyText:
European football body UEFA has threatened FIFA with legal action over Gianni Infantino's failed plan to sell a stake in future World Cup profits to private investors, and said any potential evidence should not be destroyed.
Infantino's secretive proposal to raise $4.2 billion from investors including the New York investment firm of Joshua Kushner was dropped early on Saturday (August 1, 2026), days after the revelation in media reports provoked a global furor.
UEFA led the backlash and on Thursday (July 30) its 55 member federations met to agree boycotting all FIFA events and competitions while the proposal was active.
Now lawyers for UEFA have informed FIFA that the European body is “actively considering legal action, arbitration, and/or regulatory complaints ... arising out of and in connection with the FFE (FIFA Forward Enterprise) plan proposed by FIFA and all related matters.”
The letter dated Friday from the legal firm Dechert in New York was seen on Monday (August 3) by The Associated Press.
The letter named 18 FIFA executives who it said should retain data, documents and electronic messages as potential evidence. They include Infantino, Zurich-based chief finance officer Thomas Peyer and Arsène Wenger, the coaching great who is FIFA's head of global soccer development.
“UEFA puts you on formal notice that any destruction, deletion, alteration, concealment, or loss of relevant materials following receipt of this notice — or following any earlier date on which you were, or reasonably should have been, aware that proceedings were anticipated — may constitute spoliation of evidence,” the letter said.
Europe seeks rival candidate to lead FIFA The Swedish soccer federation confirmed on Monday (August 3) that UEFA is actively looking "to come up with an alternative candidate” as FIFA president. The next election is scheduled in March.
On Saturday (August 1), UEFA signalled it wants to end Infantino's decade-long presidency, saying he had lost the confidence of world soccer and that “no option should be off the table.”
Hours earlier, Infantino had withdrawn the divisive proposal that offered FIFA's 211 member federations one-off payments of $20 million each with a mid-September deadline to accept.
The FFE spin-off valued by FIFA at $20 billion would have taken control of the soccer body's money-making commercial and tournament operations through at least 2038. It promised to more than double development money over that time for the 211 members who already effectively own the Zurich-based not-for-profit governing body.
It was the project of just one man, FIFA's chief operating officer Kevin Lamour said in a stinging statement Friday to the AP which said staff felt deceived by their boss Infantino.
Legal proceedings are “reasonably anticipated,” UEFA's lawyer Andrew J. Levander wrote, citing the belief of soccer stakeholders that the plan was “fundamentally incompatible with the proper governance of football.” Opposition to InfantinoUEFA has been most outspoken against its former employee Infantino while the Asian Football Confederation and CONCACAF, the North and Central American and Caribbean soccer body, also have made strong statements to oppose Infantino's plan.
Infantino has most support from his traditional base in Africa, while South America's CONMEBOL is relying on him to expand the 2030 World Cup to 64 teams from 48. That would give more hosting games to Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay, the home country of CONMEBOL president Alejandro Dominguez.
Infantino's path to stabilizing the presidency he has held for 10 1/2 years was unclear on Monday (August 3) which began in New York with a report he was seeking support from the administration of his close ally U.S. President Donald Trump, possibly in a call with Secretary of State Marco Rubio.
“There are no plans for @SecRubio to speak with Infantino and there is no call this morning,” Dylan Johnson, assistant secretary of state for global public affairs, posted on social media.
The private equity plan has provoked a stunning turnaround in fortunes for Infantino since it was revealed last Tuesday (July 28) by The Times of London.
The 56-year-old FIFA leader left New York after the World Cup final two weeks ago seemingly a lock to be re-elected unopposed next March for a fourth and final term in office through 2031.
The spin-off operation could have created a commissioner-like role for him beyond 2031 paying much more than his current $6 million annual salary and bonus deal as president.
FIFA briefed at the World Cup that Infantino had got pledged letters of support from about 200 of the 211 member federations.
Those letters are now likely being withdrawn across Europe with the Wales federation the first to announce its reversal.
The candidate deadline is Nov. 18 for an election exactly four months later in Morocco, one of Infantino's strongest allies and a co-host of the 2030 tournament with Spain and Portugal.
Published - August 04, 2026 12:35 am IST

stories.headline: Chelsea lands veteran Jordan Henderson on 2-year deal after Brentford exit
stories.deck: The 36-year-old Henderson is Chelsea’s oldest signing since BlueCo took over the club in 2022
stories.bodyText:
Chelsea signed veteran England midfielder Jordan Henderson to a two-year contract on Monday (August 3, 2026) following his departure from Brentford last week.
The 36-year-old Henderson is Chelsea’s oldest signing since BlueCo took over the club in 2022.
“The midfielder, who has won eight trophies in his career, including the Premier League and UEFA Champions League, has signed a two-year contract with the Blues and will join his new team-mates ahead of the 2026-27 campaign,” Chelsea said on its website.
Henderson won the Champions League in 2019 and Premier League in 2020 with Liverpool.
“Given the size of the club, the manager (Xabi Alonso), who I have great admiration for, and the quality of the players, this was a huge opportunity I couldn’t turn down,” Henderson said. “I was also so impressed with how much the ownership want Chelsea to be successful and move in the right direction.”
Henderson’s off-season signing follows that of Danny Welbeck, Morgan Rogers, Maxence Lacroix, Marco Palestra, and Geovany Quenda by the Stamford Bridge club.
